change_log.summary: Improve memory schema and retrieval ranking for reviewer memories
details: Root cause / diagnosis: Retrieval returned noisy or insufficient context because memories lacked lightweight metadata (timestamp, relevance score, tags) and records were not ranked beyond insertion order. This reduced recall and ordering quality for same-dimension queries and made summaries less useful.

Specific change: Extend KnowledgeItem schema with timestamp (float), importance score (float), and tags (list[str]) fields. Update write() to populate these fields (compute timestamp and heuristic importance), log writes, and store records. Enhance read() to prefer same-dimension items but sort candidates by (dimension match, importance, recency) and format output more compactly while preserving the 3000 char limit.

change_log.summary: Improve memory ranking by leveraging tags and expand candidate pool
details: Root cause / diagnosis: Retrieval sometimes returned suboptimal ordering because candidate scoring relied only on dimension match, importance, and recency. It did not exploit tags embedded in memories that could strongly signal relevance to a query, and the candidate pool was modestly capped which could omit useful items.

Specific change: Add a lightweight tag-match boost (if query text mentions any memory tag) into the candidate scoring, increase the considered candidate slice slightly, and refine formatting bounds. Kept all schema types unchanged and preserved the single-LLM-call constraint.

change_log.summary: Add structured metadata, scoring, and type annotations to memory schema; improve retrieval ranking and logging
details: Diagnosis: The original MemoryProgram used untyped/underspecified dataclasses and a simple FIFO retrieval that did not leverage importance or timestamps. This limited recall precision and made retrieval less relevant for reviewer-dimension queries (contributing to rotated validation issues).

Change: Add explicit typed fields (timestamp, importance, tags) to KnowledgeItem with metadata; record these fields in writes; enhance read() to score by dimension match, importance, and recency; include lightweight tag matching and toolkit.debug logging to aid downstream diagnostics. All interfaces remain fully compatible.

change_log.summary: Enrich memory schema and make write/read more robust
details: Diagnosis: The MemoryProgram stored only a bare reviewer_dimension and preserved full raw_text; downstream components and tests expect richer structured memory items (lessons, facts, reviewer name, tags, timestamps, importance) and more robust retrieval ranking. Lack of these fields reduced retrieval relevance and caused brittle outputs. The read path relied on the LLM but fell back to unstructured history when errors occurred; overall retrieval ranking and metadata were weak.

Specific change: Extend KnowledgeItem and Query dataclasses with safe, allowed-typed metadata fields (lesson_learned, fact_to_remember, reviewer_name, timestamp, importance, tags). Update write() to normalize and store structured records and to avoid empty writes. Improve read() retrieval ranking (dimension, tag matching, importance, recency) and format top results compactly. Preserve single LLM call in read() and keep output within 3000 characters. Add defensive coding around toolkit logger and llm call.
